title: Checkmate!
summary: No escape from check means the game is over.

steps.text: CHECKMATE happens when the king is in check AND there's no way to escape — no safe square to move to, nothing to block with, and no way to capture the attacker. Look here: White's king on h1 can't escape to g2 or h2 (his own pawns are there!), and can't capture the queen on g1 (the knight on e2 is guarding it). That's checkmate — Black wins!
Check isn't always checkmate, though! Here's a similar position, but this time nothing guards the queen. The king simply captures her: Kxg1. Always look for a way out before giving up.

Or check might not be checkmate because you can block it. Imagine a rook checking all the way from e8 — the king could put another piece in between, like this bishop hopping to e5, and the check disappears.

steps.prompt: Black's king is boxed in by his own pawns! Find the move that delivers checkmate using your rook.
steps.successText: Checkmate! You trapped the king completely. Game over!
steps.retryText: The king can't escape along the back rank — slide your rook all the way up.

steps.text: Great job spotting and delivering checkmate! Checkmate ends the game instantly. Next, let's learn two special king moves: castling!
